Every value in this dataset is money, not tonnage. Revenue must never be summed with or divided into tonnes without stating the rate.

Glass other and wood are published as a single combined 'Exp & Rep' row rather than split into exporter and reprocessor. The files state the reason: releasing the split would breach EIR Regulation 12(5)(e) on the confidentiality of commercially sensitive information. The suppression is lawful and permanent, so revenue by operator type is unavailable for those two materials in every year. Any exporter-versus-reprocessor comparison covers five materials, not seven.

The 2025 file carries a stray numeric cell at row 6, column 13, holding 322,471,936 — the grand total copied into an otherwise empty far column. A spreadsheet artefact, not data. The parser reads only the mapped spend columns and reports any numeric value outside them, which is how this was found. It is excluded from the output.

The three files are not laid out identically. The header is on row 1 in 2023 and 2024 and row 2 in 2025. The row order differs: 2023 and 2024 list Reprocessor before Exporter for glass re-melt, paper, plastic and steel, while 2025 lists Exporter first. Nothing is read by row or column position; the header is found by its label and every row is keyed on the material and accreditation type it carries.

Total reported revenue was 595,564,715 pounds in 2023, 291,957,687 in 2024 and 322,471,936 in 2025 — a fall of 51.0 per cent followed by a rise of 10.5 per cent. The trajectory is not a steady decline, and the 2023 figure is nearly double either later year.
